newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: NWE bunkers rise, other areas slow to follow.
newsitem.headline: NWE bunkers rise, other areas slow to follow.

text.p: NWE fuel oil bunkers firmed sharply on Monday after expected delays to Iraqi oil exports sent crude and products prices soaring, but bunkers in other regions were slow to to follow, dealers said.

Rotterdam 380 cst rose $3 to $106/$107. Dealers said there had been a number of enquiries from shipowners and minor short-covering. However, while the barge market was active, traded volume of bunkers was low. Dealers said trading had been active last week and buyers hoped the strength was short-lived.
"They just postponed their decisions or booked their bunkers elsewhere," one dealer said.
Hamburg prices rose to around $112, the strong cargo market restoring a $5 differential between Hamburg and Rotterdam prices
Med prices were slower to respond to crude and NWE product rises with demand very thin. Dealers said bunkers should firm on Tuesday, but this prospect did little to encourage buyers.
"There's simply not enough business to justify the price rises today," one dealer said.
Durban prices firmed as one major stayed out of the market to recommission its crude furnace. Dealers said it should be running normally by the end of this week.
